These compounds, in turn, target M-phase phosphoprotein 8, suggesting a potential indirect pathway through which Tenalisib may influence this protein. The evidence is consistent across three distinct paths, with varying scores, but all pointing to a common downstream effect on M-phase phosphoprotein 8. The integration of these pathways implies that Tenalisib may modulate the activity of these kinases, which could then affect M-phase phosphoprotein 8 through phosphorylation or other regulatory mechanisms. The relationship is supported by the presence of overlapping targets and the shared involvement of M-phase phosphoprotein 8 in the downstream pathways, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
